newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to list Postbank on mkt in 98-govt sources.
newsitem.headline: Germany to list Postbank on mkt in 98-govt sources.

text.p: German government sources said on Thursday that as part of its programme to boost non-tax revenues, the privatisation of Postbank AG will take place in 1998 directly to the market.
The privatisation would therefore take place without "parking" the shares with the Kreditanstalt fuer Wiederaufbau, the sources said.
The "parking" plan had been floated as a way to realise the revenue this year, but was later shelved as the direct sale could bring in more money.
Postbank, which has always favoured a sale direct to the market, said earlier this week that there was no longer enough time for a share market listing this year.

Postbank must still decide on possible partners in the insurance and building-society sectors, and whether it will swap shares with such partners, said Hans-Gottfried Bernrath, president of the Bundesanstalt fuer Post- und Telekommunikation.
The decision will be made by early August whether to seek partners. If so, the partners will be decided by mid-September, he said.

The BHW Bausparkasse and Wuestenrot are still in contention as possible building-society partners, while Volksfuersorge, Colonia-Konzern and Allianz have expressed interest on the insurance side, Bernrath said.
Postbank now plans to go it alone in investment banking.
